content: 1. Ivosidenib and Clarithromycin: Ivosidenib reduces the effectiveness of clarithromycin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative therapies. If unavoidable, monitor for reduced therapeutic effects. 2. Clarithromycin and Ixabepilone: Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of ixabepilone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 3. Omeprazole and Ketoconazole: Omeprazole decreases the effectiveness of ketoconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 4. Clarithromycin and Ketamine: Clarithromycin increases ketamine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 5. Clarithromycin and Ketoconazole: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Ketoconazole also increases clarithromycin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 6. Clarithromycin and Lapatinib: Clarithromycin increases lapatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 7. Clarithromycin and Larotrectinib: Clarithromycin increases larotrectinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 8. Clarithromycin and Lefamulin: Clarithromycin increases lefamulin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, and both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 9. Clarithromycin and Lemborexant: Clarithromycin increases lemborexant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. Use alternative drugs if necessary. 10. Clarithromycin and Leniolisib: Clarithromycin increases leniolisib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 11. Clarithromycin and Levoketoconazole: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Omeprazole decreases levoketoconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 12. Clarithromycin and Lithium: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 13. Omeprazole and Lonafarnib: Omeprazole increases lonafarnib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce lonafarnib to its starting dose. 14. Clarithromycin and Macimorelin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Macimorelin increases the QT interval by approximately 11 milliseconds. 15. Clarithromycin and Macitentan: Clarithromycin increases macitentan levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 16. Clarithromycin and Mefloquine: Clarithromycin increases mefloquine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, and both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 17. Omeprazole and Mesalamine: Omeprazole reduces mesalamine effectiveness by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral sustained-release forms. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 18. Clarithromycin and Mestranol: Clarithromycin increases mestranol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 19. Clarithromycin and Methadone: Clarithromycin increases methadone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 20. Clarithromycin and Methylprednisolone: Clarithromycin increases methylprednisolone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 21. Clarithromycin and Midazolam: Clarithromycin increases midazolam levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Intranasal midazolam exposure may lead to prolonged sedation. 22. Clarithromycin and Mifepristone: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 23. Clarithromycin and Mirtazapine: Clarithromycin increases mirtazapine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, and both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 24. Clarithromycin and Modafinil: Clarithromycin increases modafinil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 25. Clarithromycin and Moxifloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 26. Clarithromycin and Nefazodone: Clarithromycin increases nefazodone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, and vice versa. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 27. Clarithromycin and Nelfinavir: Clarithromycin increases nelfinavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 28. Omeprazole and Nilotinib: Omeprazole reduces nilotinib levels by increasing gastric pH. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Nilotinib solubility is pH-dependent. 29. Clarithromycin and Niraparib: Clarithromycin increases niraparib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 30. Clarithromycin and Ondansetron: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. ECG monitoring is recommended in high-risk patients. 31. Clarithromycin and Osimertinib: Clarithromycin increases osimertinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 32. Clarithromycin and Oxaliplatin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 33. Clarithromycin and Oxycodone: Clarithromycin increases oxycodone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Dose reduction may be necessary. 34. Clarithromycin and Palbociclib: Clarithromycin increases palbociclib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or reduce palbociclib dose to 75 mg/day. 35. Clarithromycin and Panobinostat: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 36. Clarithromycin and Pazopanib: Clarithromycin increases pazopanib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or reduce pazopanib dose to 400 mg/day. 37. Clarithromycin and Pemigatinib: Clarithromycin increases pemigatinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or reduce pemigatinib dose as per guidelines. 38. Omeprazole and Pexidartinib: Omeprazole reduces pexidartinib levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Avoid co-administration or use H2-receptor antagonists or antacids. 39. Clarithromycin and Perphenazine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs.
